title: Uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles with regard to the protection of the occupants in the event of a frontal collision (offset deformable barrier test)
scope_summary: Approves vehicle types with regard to the protection of front-seat occupants in a frontal collision, using an offset deformable barrier test at 56 km/h with instrumented Hybrid III dummies. The requirements also cover post-crash electrical safety of high-voltage systems and hydrogen safety. It applies to M1 vehicles up to 3,500 kg and N1 vehicles up to 2,500 kg, and other vehicles may be approved at the manufacturer's request.
scope_quote: This Regulation applies to vehicles of category M1 of a total permissible mass not exceeding 3,500 kg and to vehicles of category N1 of a total permissible mass not exceeding 2,500 kg; other vehicles may be approved at the request of the manufacturer.
applies_to_components: Protective system (interior fittings and restraint devices for front-seat occupants)
Airbags, including driver and passenger airbags
Front structure of the vehicle forward of the transverse plane through the driver's R point
Passenger compartment (occupant protection: intrusion and survival space)
Steering control and steering column (dummy contact, displacement)
Front seats and seat displacement systems
Doors and door locking, including automatically activated door locking systems
Footwell and pedals (dummy foot and tibia loads)
High voltage electric power train: REESS, traction motor, electronic converters, electrical energy conversion system (e.g. fuel cell), HV bus, wiring harness, connectors, coupling system for charging
Electrical protection barriers, enclosures, solid insulators and automatic disconnect
REESS electrolyte leakage and REESS retention
Compressed hydrogen storage system (CHSS), container, shut-off valve and downstream piping (post-crash leak and enclosed-space concentration)
User instructions and warnings for airbags
relation_to_other_regulations: Vehicle categories M1/N1 are as defined in the Consolidated Resolution on the Construction of Vehicles (R.E.3), ECE/TRANS/WP.29/78/Rev.7.
The H point / R point determination procedure (Annex 6 and its appendices) refers to Addendum 6 of Mutual Resolution No. 1 (M.R.1).
Approval numbering follows Schedule 4 of the 1958 Agreement (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3).
The hydrogen fuel definition refers to ISO 14687:2019 and SAE J2719_202003.
The approval mark may be combined with the marks of other UN Regulations under which the vehicle is approved (para. 4.5).
No replaced or superseded regulations are stated in the opening sections.

An airbag assembly intended to protect occupant(s) in seats other than the driver's in a frontal collision.

A system that locks the doors automatically at a pre-set speed or other manufacturer-defined condition.
A device by which a seat or part of it can be displaced and/or rotated, without a fixed intermediate position, to give access to the space behind it.

An electrolyte not based on water as the solvent.
The condition that the maximum voltage of a galvanically connected circuit between a DC live part and any other live part is ≤ 30 V AC rms and ≤ 60 V DC.

A system storing compressed hydrogen fuel, composed of container, container attachments and primary closure devices.

applicability_hints: This is a whole-vehicle crash approval: components are not approved separately, but any part that influences frontal crash performance falls within the vehicle type and its extension rules.

Changes to the front structure forward of the transverse plane through the driver's R point, or to the vehicle's length, width or unladen mass, can affect approval and may require extension or retesting.

Any restraint-related interior fitting is part of the 'protective system', and a change in its technology, geometry or materials is a different protective system type. This includes seat belts, airbags, steering wheel or column, dashboard padding, knee bolsters and seats.
Vehicles equipped with airbags, including passenger airbags, must meet the user instruction and warning requirements of para. 6.
Seat mechanisms with easy-entry displacement systems, door latches and locks, and automatically activated door locking systems are assessed post-crash.

Any high voltage component (>60 V DC or >30 V AC) in the electric power train is subject to post-crash electrical safety checks: protection against direct and indirect contact, isolation resistance, low energy or voltage, electrolyte leakage and REESS retention. This includes REESS, inverters, DC/DC converters, e-motors, HV harnesses and connectors, the charging inlet and fuel cells.
A 12 V or 48 V auxiliary or starter battery is not a REESS, and circuits meeting the specific voltage condition are not part of the high voltage bus.
Hydrogen-fuelled vehicles (fuel cell or H2 ICE) bring the CHSS, container, shut-off valve and downstream piping into scope for post-crash leak and enclosed-space hydrogen concentration limits.
The location of the REESS and the CHSS configuration are vehicle-type criteria, so relocating them may create a new vehicle type.
Fuel system integrity (post-crash fuel leakage) is assessed, so fuel tank and line routing in the front structure is relevant.
Vehicles outside M1 ≤3,500 kg or N1 ≤2,500 kg (e.g. heavier N1, M2) may still be approved voluntarily at the manufacturer's request.
